message.content: {"caption":"A structured CoWork example shows how execution evidence informs alternating model and skill updates.","description":"A green-and-white, multi-section infographic titled “Report-driven co-evolution | CoWork example.” It begins with a task to process a CSV, preserve row order, and submit checked output. A table lists two execution cases: at S3, the row-order check is skipped and there is no test output, although the required skill exists; at S4, after a restart, trial-results.json is used without being opened, and retrieval and validation are omitted in the new workspace. An LLM-attribution note says to pool scores and traces across development tasks and exclude infrastructure failures. The LLM report targets S3 when it has the most frequent model-attributed failures, identifies a skipped known verification procedure, and requests prioritizing S3 practice while retaining adjacent stages and end-to-end tasks. The harness report identifies the missing post-restart artifact check and recommends retrieving, opening, and validating saved output, with recovery attempts before reporting an unavailable artifact. Lower panels describe separate model-update and skill-update procedures, with acceptance gates and rejection actions. A final strip says to evaluate the retained pair, regenerate reports, and alternate the update axis in the next round.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
